summary: Steel Aermotor lookout on Slide Mountain, Fremont NF: built 1929, towers sold for scrap in 1968, gone by 1973. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 47-foot Aermotor LX-25 all-steel tower with a 7x7 cab
facts.status_note: Steel tower sold for scrap in 1968; cab and cabin gone by 1973.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Fremont National Forest

events.note: Telephone line to the peak completed August 20 (September 1925 item); erection of a lookout there mentioned
47-foot Aermotor steel tower with 7x7 cab, replacing a 1920s 20-foot platform
One-room 14 by 16 ft cabin built for living quarters
16 by 18 ft garage built; later dismantled and moved to Paisley
District Ranger memo gives tower height as 48 feet
John Strang Jr. serving as Forest Service lookout (Bend Bulletin, July 1943)
All improvements except the tower removed
May 1968 letter: towers offered to Army, to be pushed over and scrap sold; October 1968 memo: sold for scrap, not yet removed
Cab and cabin gone by 1973 (register); firelookout.com says gone 1973

evidence.supports: 20-foot 1920s platform replaced in 1929 by 47-foot Aermotor tower; cab and cabin gone by 1973
evidence.quote: A 20' platform built in the 1920s was replaced in 1929 with a 47' Aermotor steel tower with 7'x7' cab and a cabin, which were gone by 1973.

evidence.supports: 1929 tower erected at $1,022.09, 47-foot Aermotor with 7x7 cab
evidence.quote: 1929: A 47-foot all steel Aermotor model LX-25 lookout tower with a steel 7x7 cab erected at a total cost of $1,022.09.

evidence.supports: September 1925 item: telephone line completed August 20 and linked to a lookout erection
evidence.quote: The Slide Mountain telephone line was completed August 20, and a phone installed. The completion of these two lines with the erection of a lookout on Slide Mountain gives the Fremont a better fire detection and communication system. (Six-Twenty-Six, September, 1925)

evidence.supports: firelookout.com gives a 5x5 cab and gone 1973
evidence.quote: 1929: 47' steel tower w/ 5x5' cab, cabin. Gone 1973.

evidence.supports: Slide Mountain is in Lake County, Fremont National Forest
evidence.quote: LAKE COUNTY SLIDE MOUNTAIN Fremont National Forest

evidence.supports: 1930 one-room 14 by 16 cabin for living quarters
evidence.quote: 1930: A one-room 14' by 16' cabin built for living quarters.

evidence.supports: 1933 16 by 18 garage later dismantled and moved to Paisley
evidence.quote: 1933: A 16' by 18' garage built. At a later date it was dismantled and moved to Paisley.

evidence.supports: 1942 memo gives tower height as 48 feet
evidence.quote: 1942: A memo from the District Ranger to the Forest Supervisor shows that the tower is 48 feet tall.

evidence.supports: July 1943 Bend Bulletin item: John Strang Jr. serving as Forest Service lookout
evidence.quote: July 13, 1943: John Strang, Jr., who has been serving as look-out on Slide mountain for the forest service, is here for a week's visit with his parents, Mr. and Mrs. John Strang. (The Bend Bulletin)

evidence.supports: by 1956 all improvements except the tower removed
evidence.quote: 1956: All improvements at Slide Mountain have been removed except for the tower which has no shutters.

evidence.supports: May 1968 letter from the Fremont National Forest
evidence.quote: May 13, 1968: A letter to the Regional office from the Fremont National Forest.

evidence.supports: towers offered to the Army last fall; Army would not take them; plan to push over, unbolt steel, and attempt to sell scrap metal
evidence.quote: Slide Mountain and Shoestring are both steel towers which were offered to the Army last fall. Since we are now advised they will not be taken, we plan to push them over and unbolt the steel members this summer. We will attempt to sell the scrap metal.

evidence.supports: October 1968 memo: sold for scrap, not yet removed
evidence.quote: October 23, 1968: A memorandum from the Forest Engineer to the Regional Forester. We have sold Shoestring and Slide Mountain steel Lookout towers for scrap. The towers have not yet been removed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the Forest Lookouts history give a 7 by 7 foot cab; firelookout.com gives 5 by 5. The story reports both and uses 7 by 7 feet, which two sources give.
The 1929 record gives 47 feet (14.3 m); a 1942 memo gives 48 feet. The story reports the 47-foot figure and notes the memo.

sources.title: History of the Fremont National Forest

notes_for_editor: No source describes the site today, so the story says so; it is not known whether the site is public. The 1973 end date comes only from the register and firelookout.com. Cab size disagrees (7x7 vs 5x5). Do not confuse this with the Slide Mountain tower above Pyramid Lake in the Los Padres (christopherplord.blogspot.com, 2018), which is a different site. The record's access is unknown and no visit facts were found.
